description:
FOUND s439 (Fable review of s438f/#435) by probe; PRE-EXISTING (identical on a
d0b52e9 worktree) and NOT the #435 mechanism -- #435 is the fragment re-parse;
this is the regex consumer's SCAN.

  use utf8; binmode STDOUT, ":utf8";
  my @Ｘ = (10,20,30); my $ｉ = 1;
  my $u = "aＸb"; $u =~ s/Ｘ/$ｉ/;         print "$u\n";   # perl: a1b   PCL: a$ｉb   (literal!)
  my $t = "aＸb"; $t =~ s/Ｘ/$Ｘ[1]/;      print "$t\n";   # perl: a20b  PCL: a$Ｘ[1]b
  my $v = "aＸb"; $v =~ s/Ｘ/${ｉ}/;       print "$v\n";   # perl: a1b   PCL: a1b    (braced form WORKS)
  my $s = "aXb";  $s =~ s/X/$X[$i]/;       # ASCII: right
  print "$Ｘ[$ｉ]";                        # dq string: right (the #435 fix)

SILENT WRONG: the replacement text goes out with the source characters in it.
The discriminator to measure first: Pl/InterpScan.pm scans with `\w` (Unicode-
aware on a CHARACTER string), and the dq-string path is right, so the
replacement text most likely reaches the scanner as undecoded BYTES (or the scan
runs under an ASCII class at that one site) -- `use utf8` decoding happens at
the source-document level (Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t); find where the s///
replacement text is taken from the PPI token and whether it is decoded there.
Rule 11: it must be the SAME scanner entry (InterpScan scan_one) the dq string
uses, with the same text encoding -- not a second class.

BAR: the four probes above as Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t rows (three positive, the
ASCII inverse), corpus-diff + 951-file A/B (expected IDENTICAL -- no population
has the shape), gate.  tr/// and the m// pattern side: probe them in the same
session (the pattern side is InterpScan's regex consumer too).


DONE s443g (Opus, agent G round 4), commit a31aad4, ff-merged s444.  The task hypothesis (undecoded bytes) KILLED by measurement -- text arrives decoded; the bug was _replacement_interpolates' private ASCII class, now answered by Pl::InterpScan::scan (braced spelling always lambda; bare magic never -- $1..$9 stay on the backref rewrite; punctuation magics still literal = #520, two-sided).  $::qq / $#arr / escaped-sigil fixed too.  Fable re-probed the family incl. $1 and \$x inverses -- identical to perl.
subject: The s/// REPLACEMENT side does not interpolate a NON-ASCII identifier at all: `s/Ｘ/$ｉ/` writes the literal `$ｉ` (dq strings and `${ｉ}` are right)
